planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall into humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade, where the clump slowly thickens into an 18-inch-tall, three-foot-wide stand.

directions: Cherry Blossom is a 2011 Plant Delights/Juniper Level Botanic Garden introduction selected from Epimedium grandiflorum seedlings, forming a vigorous clump of fresh green foliage. In early spring, wiry stems rise above the leaves bearing cherry-red flowers, each flanked by contrasting white spurs that give the blooms a bicolor, butterfly-like look. Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade, where the clump slowly thickens to about 18 inches tall and three feet wide. Once established it tolerates competition from tree roots and short dry spells, though flowering is best with consistent spring moisture.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into evenly moist, humus-rich soil in partial sun to light shade, allowing room for arching two-foot flower stalks to display without crowding.

directions: Golden Angels is a Plant Delights/JLBG release selected from a semi-evergreen seedling population, prized for its unusually long, arching flower stalks. In spring the two-foot stems bend outward under the weight of large, dangling, clear yellow flowers held well above the foliage. The clump matures to about 18 inches tall and three feet wide, spreading slowly into a dense patch in partial sun to light shade. Grow in humus-rich, evenly moist soil and leave the semi-evergreen foliage in place through winter for extra-early spring interest.

planting.note: Plant divisions in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun to light shade; mulch with leaf litter to keep roots cool through summer heat.

directions: Yellowstone is a Plant Delights/JLBG hybrid selected for exceptional vigor and an unusually long bloom season. Beginning in mid-March, each clump sends up abundant spikes of dangling, clear yellow flowers that continue for roughly ten weeks, far outlasting most fairy wings. The clump spreads at a moderate pace in partial sun to light shade and tolerates dry shade once established. Plant divisions in humus-rich, well-drained soil and give it a season to settle in before expecting full flower output.

planting.note: Plant divisions in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun to light shade, and cut back last year's foliage in late winter so new leaf color is not obscured.

directions: Dark Beauty is a chance hybrid of Epimedium grandiflorum 'Yubae' and 'Silver Queen' that arose in the garden of the late plantsman Harold Epstein, chosen for dark, chocolate-purple spring foliage that later greens up as temperatures rise. In spring the foot-tall clump produces purple-and-white bicolor flowers that carry a light citrus fragrance noticeable in the afternoon. Plant divisions in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun to light shade, where it forms a deer- and rabbit-resistant groundcover over several seasons. Cut back the previous year's foliage in late winter so the new leaf color and flowers are not obscured.

planting.note: Divide and plant in spring or fall into humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial sun to shade for the most reliable establishment.

directions: Silver Queen is an uncommon Epimedium grandiflorum selection that has often been confused in the trade with the similarly named White Queen. New growth emerges a warm cinnamon color in late March before fading to green as the season warms, and short stalks lift large white flowers blushed with lilac just above the foliage. The clump reaches roughly a foot tall and spreads slowly in part sun to shade. Give it humus-rich, evenly moist soil and propagate by division in spring or fall.

planting.note: Plant divisions in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun to light shade, giving the clump several feet of room to widen over time.

directions: Lyrical Lemonade is a 2023 Plant Delights/JLBG introduction of a Hans Hansen hybrid, grown as much for its long, well-branched flower spikes as for its tight semi-evergreen foliage. From late March into April, the clump produces abundant bright yellow, spidery flowers whose narrow sepals give them an airy, spreading look. In time the clump widens to roughly four feet across in partial sun to light shade. Plant divisions in humus-rich, well-drained soil and expect the slow but steady spread typical of clump-forming fairy wings.

planting.note: Plant divisions in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun to light shade and leave evergreen foliage in place through winter where climate allows.

directions: Rise and Shine is a Plant Delights/JLBG Epimedium introduction notable for glossy, evergreen foliage, often forked at the leaf tips and edged in red as it emerges. Large, spider-shaped flowers open ivory with an amber cup in late March and gradually age to amber-pink, creating a two-toned effect across the bloom season. The compact clump reaches about a foot tall and just over two feet wide in partial sun to light shade. Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil and leave the evergreen leaves in place through winter wherever temperatures stay mild enough.

planting.note: Plant divisions in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun to light shade; this clone holds evergreen foliage further north than most x rubrum selections.

directions: Sweetheart is an Epimedium x rubrum selection bred by Darrell Probst, selected for foliage that stays fully evergreen even in northern gardens. New leaves emerge heavily flushed red in spring, creating a colorful show before bright pink flowers open on wiry stems. The clump spreads slowly into a dense, weed-suppressing patch in partial sun to light shade. Plant divisions in humus-rich, well-drained soil and expect reliable winter foliage color further north than most x rubrum selections.

planting.note: Plant divisions in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade; tight clumping habit suits path edges and small shade gardens.

directions: Snowshoe Lake is a 2014 Cobblewood Gardens selection of the Japanese species Epimedium sempervirens, valued as one of the earliest fairy wings to flower, often opening by the third week of February. The evergreen clump produces a dense show of large, pure white flowers held just above tidy foliage, maturing to about a foot tall and two feet wide. Grow in light shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil, where its tight clumping habit makes it useful near paths or in small shade gardens. Leave the evergreen leaves through winter for the earliest possible bloom display.

planting.note: Give divisions ample room in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun to light shade, since this is one of the larger epimediums grown.

directions: Spring Sunrise is a Plant Delights/JLBG introduction with Epimedium wushanense in its parentage, inheriting that species' long, horizontally branched flower spikes, which here exceed 15 inches. The evergreen leaves emerge heavily mottled purple toward the center before fading to green, and the clump can reach an imposing size in full flower. Blooms are bicolor, pairing a light yellow outer spur with a darker yellow inner cup touched with brown, peaking in early April with scattered rebloom into late May. Give it room to spread in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun to light shade.

planting.note: Plant divisions in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun to light shade; spread is moderate rather than aggressive, making it easy to contain.

directions: Sunny and Share is a 2012 Plant Delights introduction, originally trialed under the designation PDN 05-018 and thought to carry Epimedium platypetalum in its background. Its evergreen foliage is lightly flecked with bronze, and the plant is notable for one of the longest bloom seasons of any epimedium, with yellow flowers appearing from late March well into midsummer. Over about five years a single division thickens into a dense, evergreen patch several feet wide. Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun to light shade, where its moderate rather than aggressive spread makes it easy to contain.

planting.note: Plant divisions in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun to light shade and give it room to range, since it spreads faster than most wushanense selections.

directions: Royal Dress is a selection of the large-leaved Chinese species Epimedium wushanense, chosen for emerging foliage in a glossy chocolate-brown that matures to green, elongated leaflets with ruffled, spiny edges. Spring flowers are bicolor, combining creamy outer spurs with a medium yellow cup, held above the foliage on wiry stems. It spreads faster than many epimediums, forming an evergreen groundcover within a few years. Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun to light shade and give it room to range.

planting.note: Divide and plant in constantly shaded, humus-rich soil that stays evenly moist, mulching with leaf litter as for other Asian wild gingers.

directions: Ichang Lemon is a Plant Delights/JLBG albino-flowered selection of the Chinese species Asarum ichangense. In late winter it produces clusters of small, creamy yellow flowers at ground level, in place of the maroon tones typical of most wild gingers. The semi-evergreen, plain green foliage stays low and spreads gradually to form a loose groundcover. Grow in light shade to shade in humus-rich soil that stays evenly moist, and mulch with leaf litter as for other Asian Asarum species.

planting.note: Plant divisions in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade to shade, where it tolerates dry shade once established.

directions: Aquarius is a Plant Delights selection of Asarum kiusianum var. tubulosum collected from Kyushu, Japan, grown for evergreen leaves patterned with fine silver veining over a green background. In early May it produces small, light beige flowers with a distinctive purple eye ring, carried at ground level beneath the foliage. The clump stays low and spreads to form a tight patch over time. Site it in light shade to shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil, where it tolerates dry shade once established.

planting.note: Divide established clumps and plant in partial sun to light shade in humus-rich soil for a reliably patterned, easy-care groundcover.

directions: Saddleback is a Plant Delights/JLBG introduction of Asarum kurosawae, selected for heart-shaped evergreen leaves patterned with a green border and central green streak set against broad silver markings. Dusty purple flowers appear low beneath the foliage starting in late November, extending the wild-ginger bloom season well past most other species. The clump stays compact, forming one of the easiest and most elegant patterned Asarum to grow. Plant in partial sun to light shade in humus-rich soil, dividing established clumps to propagate.

planting.note: Plant divisions in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial sun to light shade, mulching with leaf litter as for other Asian wild gingers.

directions: Netscape is a Plant Delights/JLBG introduction of Asarum nobilissimum, named for the fine, net-like pattern of silver veins across its large, glossy green leaves. Oversized purple flowers spotted with yellow open at ground level in late April and early May, among the showiest blooms in the genus. The lightly stoloniferous clump spreads gradually into a broader patch over a decade or more. Grow in partial sun to light shade in humus-rich, evenly moist soil, mulching with leaf litter as for other Asian wild gingers.

planting.note: Plant divisions in humus-rich soil in partial sun to light shade; divide in spring or fall to increase stock of this patterned-leaf selection.

directions: Super Shield is a Plant Delights/JLBG introduction notable because Asarum nobilissimum is almost always offered as solid green-leaved forms; this selection instead carries bold silver patterning across its evergreen foliage. Purple flowers speckled with yellow open in April at ground level beneath the patterned leaves. The clump spreads slowly by short stolons into a tidy patch. Plant in partial sun to light shade in humus-rich soil, and divide clumps in spring or fall to increase stock.

planting.note: Plant divisions in light shade to shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil typical of woodland Asarum culture.

directions: Suzaku Botan is a rare Japanese selection of Asarum rigescens var. brachypodion, also known in collections as 'Ise-jishi', distinguished by flowers that are uniquely double, resembling a miniature rose rather than the typical single bell of most wild gingers. The tan-and-lavender blooms appear at ground level in January and February, well ahead of most other Asarum. Arrow-shaped, fragrant evergreen leaves carry large, ornate silver blotches over green, forming a tight clump. Grow in light shade to shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil typical of woodland Asarum culture.

planting.note: Plant divisions in light shade to shade in humus-rich, evenly moist soil; expect fall rather than spring flowering from this unusual selection.

directions: Tama Rasya is a Japanese Asarum selection notable for flowering in mid-October, well outside the late-winter to spring season typical of most wild gingers. Its arrow-shaped evergreen leaves are a dusty light green overlaid with muted silver patterning and scattered small white dots, giving the foliage a frosted look year-round. Soft yellow flowers open at ground level in fall on a low, clumping mound. Plant in light shade to shade in humus-rich, evenly moist soil, where it forms tidy evergreen clumps over time.
